question.text: The interest rate parity theory states that:

answer.text: The difference between forward and spot exchange rates is approximately equal to the interest rate differential between the two currencies
Interest rates in all countries must be equal
Higher interest rate currencies always appreciate in the spot market
Forward rates are always higher than spot rates

explanation.text: The Logic: Interest rate parity states F/S = (1+RQC)/(1+RBC). The forward premium or discount reflects the interest rate differential between the two currencies, producing an arbitrage-free relationship between spot and forward exchange rates. The Trap: Forward rates can be lower than spot if the base currency has a higher interest rate than the quote currency. Note: When INR interest rates exceed USD interest rates, INR trades at a forward discount to USD and USDINR futures trade at a premium to spot.
